newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end lower after fierce battle. [CORRECTED 11:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end lower after fierce battle. [CORRECTED 11:35 GMT]

text.p: Tokyo stocks ended lower in the Monday session, after the key Nikkei index battled fiercely to avoid sinking past the 20,000 level on pressure from the Dow which weakened on Friday, brokers said. They said trade was thin and centred around speculative, incentive-backed shares.
The 225-issue benchmark Nikkei lost 59.79 points or 0.30 percent to close at 20,107.11 (corrects closing figure from 21,107.11). Its September futures shed 20 points to settle at 20,150.
"The Nikkei average was in a tug-of-war state for most of the day near the 20,000 level," said Harushige Kobayashi, deputy general manager at Yamaichi Securities.
Brokers said waves of profit-taking in Takefuji shares helped lower the over-the-counter (OTC) index. The index ended down 11.62 points or 0.73 percent at 1,569.84.
Takefuji which had the largest trade volume in the OTC at 1.14 million shares, debuted last Friday with a 10,200 strike price. But the share price crumbled to 9,630 yen by the session's end.

Promise, another personal loan company, fell 360 yen in tandem with Takefuji to stand at 5,090 yen, ranking second on the first section of the Tokyo exchange's largest percent loss list. Turnover was 225,700 shares.
Speculative issues were at the top of the list of most heavily trade volumes on the first section, indicating how dull trade was, brokers said.
Mitsui Matsushima was down 10 yen at 715 yen with turnover of 5.859 million shares. TYK Corp was down 80 yen at 1,490 yen on volume of 5.469 million.
Losers outnumbered winners 621 issues to 378 issues with 231 issues unchanged.
Sector-wise, insurance, foods, land transport, oil and warehouses were the leading gainers.
Communications, textiles, sea transportation, real estate and air services were the leading retreating sectors.
